\begin{tablenotes}
Panel A: sequential steps from the 173 verified open-weight base models, with the audited token counts (StableLM-Alpha
at 0.8 trillion tokens and MPT-30B at 1.05 trillion; Online Appendix~\ref{app:choices}); each row describes the sample
that remains after the step, and a model is dropped at the first step that applies. Reference technology: the Chinchilla
form with the outer exponent free (inner exponents 0.424 and 0.431, $\sigma^*_\kappa=0.701$), in total parameters.
$s=(w-1)/w$. All points $>1$: every one of the 32 technologies of Table~\ref{tab:app-technologies} puts the point
estimate above one. Band $>1$: the union of the 95 percent intervals over those technologies lies above one. With the
token counts of the previous version the all-points share of the clean sample was 0.64; the StableLM-Alpha correction puts
StableLM-Alpha 3B below one under MiniCPM's law, which lowers it to 0.62. Last column: the median under the Chinchilla
form with $\kappa=1$. Groups: families, except developers in the serving, target and tier rows of Panel~B. Panel~B, first
four rows: members of a family whose token budgets are within 10 percent of each other form one decision (Online
Appendix~\ref{app:wedge-family}). Synthetic data: the earlier flag drops the nine models of phi-1.5, phi-2 and SmolLM 1--3;
$^b$the protocol's rule flags every decision whose report documents teacher-generated data in pretraining or mid-training
(21 of the 49 decisions, with 38 models, including all six decisions of 2025). $^a$A first-party per-token API or consumer
product offered this size within 180 days of release (Online Appendix~\ref{app:choices}). Tier windows: 2.4--3.3,
6.5--9.5, 11.5--14.9, 26--32.9 and 65--72.9 billion parameters, where a binding tier's shadow value is part of the value
of compactness.
\end{tablenotes}
